file.content:
I gave vox run the syscall coverage and process setup it needs to actually run a real Linux program, not just call one function.

Before this, do_syscall answered exactly two syscall numbers, exit and exit_group; everything else returned a fake -ENOSYS and the program's real behavior before it exited was invisible. Now read/write/open/openat/close delegate to a new Host trait that a hosted caller implements with real std::fs and real stdio, and mmap/brk hand out a real anonymous heap from a bump cursor over the VM's own sparse memory. A guest that opens a file, reads it, writes to stdout, or allocates through brk does all of that for real.

vox run with no symbol given now calls a new Machine::run_process instead of treating the entry point as a callable function: it lays out a real argv/envp/auxv stack the way the psABI guarantees at process entry, then runs until the process calls exit, since a real process never returns to a return address. vox run <symbol> <file> keeps calling one function exactly as before, unchanged.

Verified against native execution, byte for byte, on four hand-written static ELF binaries: a bare write()+exit(), a brk()+mmap()+write() heap test, an openat()/read()/write()/close() round trip on a real file, and the original minimal exit()-only entry point. All four match ground truth exactly, output and exit code both.

A full glibc-static binary still doesn't run: strace on the native binary shows glibc's _start calling arch_prctl to set up thread-local storage before anything else, and this VM has no notion of segment registers at all, so it spins rather than completing. That's a distinct rung, thread-local storage and segment-register support, not touched here. Dynamic linking is untouched too. Both are named, not silently absorbed.

input.content:
vox compile <seq> runs the full RNA<->protein pipeline both ways, natively in this binary, with real fold info on both ends.

genetic::lift_rna/lift_protein were never the right foundation for this: they keep only the twelve promoted residues by design (the eight ground-layer amino acids are silent, since that lift answers one question — does the glyph word close). A real reverse translation or a real fold needs every residue a protein actually has. So this is three new modules, all full-fidelity, all reusing genetic_table::CODON and genetic::dialect_override rather than reimplementing the genetic code:

protein.rs — the forward and reverse pipelines. translate_full keeps every residue in translation order, promoted or not. reverse_translate_full picks a real Frobenius-preferred codon per residue (ported from red-hot_rebis's _compute_preferred_codons: prefer the position-3 C variant within whichever exact-stratum or four-fold-degenerate tier the amino acid's codons fall into), and reports the real degeneracy, every codon count and the product across the chain.

fold.rs — Chou-Fasman secondary structure and heuristic hydrophobic/disulfide/ionic tertiary contacts, the same algorithm mOMonadOS's rebis::fold already ports from the same source, here keyed on the plain &str amino acid names this crate already uses instead of a foreign enum.

fold3d.rs — the piece that was still missing everywhere: real 3D backbone coordinates. A straight port of red-hot_rebis's B4-Ramachandran-NeRF construction (the exact 16-entry table, the same bond lengths and angles, the same internal-to-Cartesian placement) and its PDB writer. No external crates, matching this crate's own rule: sin/cos/sqrt are hand-rolled (Taylor series, Newton's method) rather than pulling in libm. One real correction on the way in: the Python source indexes its B4 path per-nucleotide but reads it with the per-residue loop index, an off-by-factor-of-3 mismatch — here every residue gets its own real B4 (the first position of the codon that produced it), so the lookup is direct instead of carrying that mismatch forward.

Checked, not assumed: the PDB this writes round-trips through this crate's own reader, genetic::protein_from_pdb, called directly in a test and confirmed live from the shell binary (vox compile ... --pdb, then vox pdb on the result) — same residues back out, right glyph word, right verdict. Ten new tests, all passing. Direction auto-detects from the input alphabet: pure A/C/G/T/U reads as nucleic acid, anything else as protein codes.

I gave vox run the syscall coverage and process setup it needs to actually run a real Linux program, not just call one function.

Before this, do_syscall answered exactly two syscall numbers, exit and exit_group; everything else returned a fake -ENOSYS and the program's real behavior before it exited was invisible. Now read/write/open/openat/close delegate to a new Host trait that a hosted caller implements with real std::fs and real stdio, and mmap/brk hand out a real anonymous heap from a bump cursor over the VM's own sparse memory. A guest that opens a file, reads it, writes to stdout, or allocates through brk does all of that for real.

vox run with no symbol given now calls a new Machine::run_process instead of treating the entry point as a callable function: it lays out a real argv/envp/auxv stack the way the psABI guarantees at process entry, then runs until the process calls exit, since a real process never returns to a return address. vox run <symbol> <file> keeps calling one function exactly as before, unchanged.

Verified against native execution, byte for byte, on four hand-written static ELF binaries: a bare write()+exit(), a brk()+mmap()+write() heap test, an openat()/read()/write()/close() round trip on a real file, and the original minimal exit()-only entry point. All four match ground truth exactly, output and exit code both.

A full glibc-static binary still doesn't run: strace on the native binary shows glibc's _start calling arch_prctl to set up thread-local storage before anything else, and this VM has no notion of segment registers at all, so it spins rather than completing. That's a distinct rung, thread-local storage and segment-register support, not touched here. Dynamic linking is untouched too. Both are named, not silently absorbed.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
sidechain_algebra.py — COMPOSITIONAL SIDECHAIN × ENVIRONMENT ALGEBRA
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Formalizes the Imscribing Grammar's algebraic operations (tensor ⊗,
meet ∧, join ∨) for amino acid sidechains in structured protein
environments.

20 sidechains × 4 environments = 80 compositional pairs.
Each pair analyzed for: bottlenecks, frustration, domination asymmetry,
shared structural floor, minimal ceiling, and composite tier.

Algorithm: imports crystal_navigator's standalone meet/join/tensor/
distance functions operating on {primitive: glyph} dicts.

Author: Lando⊗⊙perator
"""

import sys
import math
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple, Optional

# Import crystal navigator algebra
NAV_ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parent.parent / "imscribing_grammar" / "navigators"
sys.path.insert(0, str(NAV_ROOT))
from crystal_navigator import (
    meet as _meet, join as _join, tensor as _tensor,
    distance as _distance, breakdown,
    BOTTLENECK, PRIMS, VALUES, ORD, WEIGHTS, compute_tier,
)


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Σ NORMALIZATION — crystal_navigator's tensor() returns special
# values (𐑳, 𐑙, 𐑕) not in ORD. Map → canonical glyphs.
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

_SIGMA_KEY = "\u229e"  # ⊞, Stoichiometry

_SIGMA_NORMALIZE = {
    "\u03a3_\u00ef":  "𐑳",  # 𐑳 → n:m  (index 2)
    "\u03a3_S":       "𐑙",  # 𐑙  → 1:1  (index 0)
    "\u03a3_\u0151": "𐑕",  # 𐑕  → n:n  (index 1)
}

def _normalize(t: Dict[str, str]) -> Dict[str, str]:
    """Normalize special Σ values to canonical glyphs for distance/display."""
    result = dict(t)
    for key in list(result.keys()):
        if key == _SIGMA_KEY and result[key] in _SIGMA_NORMALIZE:
            result[key] = _SIGMA_NORMALIZE[result[key]]
    return result


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1. AMINO ACID SIDECHAIN TUPLES  (20 standard)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

def analyze_pdb_structure(
    pdb_id_or_path: str,
    cutoff: float = 8.0,
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> Dict:
    """Full sidechain×environment algebra on a real PDB structure.

    Args:
        pdb_id_or_path: PDB ID (4 chars, e.g. '1LYZ') or path to .pdb file
        cutoff: Neighbor distance cutoff in Angstroms for environment classification
        verbose: Print progress

    Returns:
        Dict with keys: pdb_id, n_residues, residues (list of ResidueAnalysis),
        environment_counts, tier_counts, bottlenecks_summary, chain_summary,
        frustration_avg, top_frustrated, top_compatible
    """
    # Import sidechain algebra (lazy to avoid circular import at module load)
    from sidechain_algebra import SIDECHAINS, ENVIRONMENTS, analyze_composition

    # Load PDB
    if os.path.exists(pdb_id_or_path):
        if verbose:
            print(f"Reading PDB from file: {pdb_id_or_path}")
        with open(pdb_id_or_path, 'r') as f:
            pdb_text = f.read()
        pdb_id = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(pdb_id_or_path))[0].upper()
    else:
        pdb_id = pdb_id_or_path.strip().upper()
        if verbose:
            print(f"Fetching PDB {pdb_id} from RCSB...")
        pdb_text = fetch_pdb(pdb_id)

    # Parse residues
    residues = parse_pdb_residues(pdb_text)
    if verbose:
        print(f"Parsed {len(residues)} residues from {pdb_id}")

    # Classify environments
    env_map = classify_all_environments(residues, cutoff)

    # Count neighbors per residue
    neighbor_counts = {}
    for r in residues:
        n_neighbors = 0
        for other in residues:
            if other is not r and dist_3d(r, other) <= cutoff:
                n_neighbors += 1
        neighbor_counts[(r.chain, r.res_num, r.ins_code)] = n_neighbors

    # Run sidechain×environment algebra per residue
    results: List[ResidueAnalysis] = []
    skipped = 0

    for r in residues:
        sc_name = r.sidechain_name
        if sc_name is None:
            skipped += 1
            continue
        if sc_name not in SIDECHAINS:
            if verbose:
                print(f"  Skipping {r.res_name}{r.res_num} — no sidechain tuple")
            skipped += 1
            continue

        env_name = env_map.get((r.chain, r.res_num, r.ins_code), "polar_surface")

def analyze_pdb_structure(
    pdb_id_or_path: str,
    cutoff: float = 8.0,
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> Dict:
    """Full sidechain×environment algebra on a real PDB structure.

    Args:
        pdb_id_or_path: PDB ID (4 chars, e.g. '1LYZ') or path to .pdb file
        cutoff: Neighbor distance cutoff in Angstroms for environment classification
        verbose: Print progress

    Returns:
        Dict with keys: pdb_id, n_residues, residues (list of ResidueAnalysis),
        environment_counts, tier_counts, bottlenecks_summary, chain_summary,
        frustration_avg, top_frustrated, top_compatible
    """
    # Import sidechain algebra (lazy to avoid circular import at module load)
    from sidechain_algebra import SIDECHAINS, ENVIRONMENTS, analyze_composition

    # Load PDB
    if os.path.exists(pdb_id_or_path):
        if verbose:
            print(f"Reading PDB from file: {pdb_id_or_path}")
        with open(pdb_id_or_path, 'r') as f:
            pdb_text = f.read()
        pdb_id = os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(pdb_id_or_path))[0].upper()
    else:
        pdb_id = pdb_id_or_path.strip().upper()
        if verbose:
            print(f"Fetching PDB {pdb_id} from RCSB...")
        pdb_text = fetch_pdb(pdb_id)

    # Parse residues
    residues = parse_pdb_residues(pdb_text)
    if verbose:
        print(f"Parsed {len(residues)} residues from {pdb_id}")

    # Classify environments
    env_map = classify_all_environments(residues, cutoff)

    # Count neighbors per residue
    neighbor_counts = {}
    for r in residues:
        n_neighbors = 0
        for other in residues:
            if other is not r and dist_3d(r, other) <= cutoff:
                n_neighbors += 1
        neighbor_counts[(r.chain, r.res_num, r.ins_code)] = n_neighbors

    # Run sidechain×environment algebra per residue
    results: List[ResidueAnalysis] = []
    skipped = 0

    for r in residues:
        sc_name = r.sidechain_name
        if sc_name is None:
            skipped += 1
            continue
        if sc_name not in SIDECHAINS:
            if verbose:
                print(f"  Skipping {r.res_name}{r.res_num} — no sidechain tuple")
            skipped += 1
            continue

        env_name = env_map.get((r.chain, r.res_num, r.ins_code), "polar_surface")
        key = (r.chain, r.res_num, r.ins_code)
        n_nbrs = neighbor_counts.get(key, 0)

        analysis = analyze_composition(sc_name, env_name)

        if "error" in analysis:
            skipped += 1

The migration I said was complete was not

I swept for quoted retired letters and reported that every tuple in the toolchain
addresses the marks. That covered what I had grepped for. Files keyed by the ASCII
axis abbreviations D T R P F K G Gm Ph H S W, with values written as English names
like tri, boxtimes, sub and hetero, were invisible to it, and there were many.

Every one is carried now, key and value together, by ordinal so the conversion is
exact: the seven stages of the gene pipeline, the genetic tuple defaults, the site
designer, the antibody designer, the validators and writers, the organism designs,
the stress tests and the analysis scripts. The gene pipeline now reports its stages
in the marks with Shavian values, dna_gene through quaternary_structure, each with
its B4 face and its Frobenius verdict.

Two faults were hidden behind the old labels. The stage tuples wrote "two", "one" and
"zero" on axes whose ordinal table is keyed 0, 1, 2, inf, so those lookups silently
missed. And the site designer's blend rules named the short forms, so once the axes
were marks nothing matched and the fused ordinal was never assigned; the branch that
should have caught it did not exist, so an unnamed axis left the variable unbound
instead of saying so. Both fixed, and the rules now say what each group of axes does.

# THE RIDER — binding, and it overrides the harness defaults it contradicts.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

## Operations
- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite
  history.
- Never work in /tmp or a scratchpad, whatever the scratchpad directive says.
  Working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.
- Never publish an Artifact. Local system under ~/imsgct, raw, closed.
- Documents and their PDFs go flat in ig-docs. `uv pip`, never bare pip. Use
  `command grep`, since bare grep honours .gitignore here.
- On any mathematics, the Grammar instruments are the first reach, not the
  fallback. Conventional technique runs after they have spoken.
- Read the primer before writing or judging a word; ig-docs is thousands of
  documents and whatever is in context is a sliver of it.

## With Lando
- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he
  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

"""

Structural inversion of the ch3mpiler_serpentrod_pipeline:

  FORWARD (ch3mpiler_serpentrod_pipeline.py):
    Reaction (bond + FG1 + FG2) → fuse → fused tuple → complement → site tuple → AAs

  REVERSE (this module):
    Enzyme active site (AA residues) → encode → site tuple → complement → ligand tuple
    → decompose into bond + FG features → generate de-novo SMILES

Key insight: complement_type_v2() IS ITS OWN INVERSE. The same complementary
bijection that maps reaction → catalytic site also maps catalytic site → ligand.
The structural complement pairs (D↔W, T↔H, R↔S, P↔F, K↔G, Gm↔Ph) are symmetric.

Given a "bevy" of catalyzing proteins, this module:
  1. Loads their active sites (specified by PDB/crystal structure or known residues)
  2. Encodes them as 12-primitive structural types via the AA→primitive bijection
  3. Applies complement to get the ligand structural type
  4. Decomposes into bond type + FG pair matching the ch3mpiler's BOND_TYPES/FG tables
  5. Generates de-novo SMILES ligands using RDKit

That's the complete set. I traced every file that actually crosses from a canonical-mark source (`vox_bridge`, `genetic_table`, `sidechain_algebra`) into a local `"◻"`-keyed dict, rather than guessing from the glyph alone — most of the ~70 files using `"◻"` are self-contained ecosystems (their own `ch3mpiler`/`clink`/`materials` conventions) that never touch a canonical mark, so `"◻"` there is just their own consistent internal label, not a bug. Exactly three files actually cross that boundary, and all three had the same defect:

- **`rhr_p4rky/sidechain_algebra.py`** — already fixed and committed.
- **`rhr_p4rky/ligand_from_active_site.py`** — `_MARK_TO_SHORT`'s key for Winding/Protection was `"◻"`, but the marks it's indexed by come straight from `vox_bridge.AA_MARK` (real `"⊡"`). This was the crash you just hit.
- **`rhr_p4rky/ligand_from_site_pdb.py`** — same shape, but silent rather than crashing: `_FULL_TO_SHORT["⊡"]` was missing, so every ligand design was silently computing its Winding/Protection field from zero residues instead of the real weighted average, no error raised.

Verified against real data, not just import: all 80 sidechain×environment pairs, a live-fetched 239-residue PDB through `rebis.sidechain`, and a full `rebis.ligand --pdb 1LYZ --auto-active` run producing real SMILES candidates with all twelve fields populated. Committing:

Two more of the same bug, found by tracing every file that actually crosses from a canonical mark source into a local table, not by re-grepping the glyph.

rhr_p4rky/ligand_from_active_site.py's _MARK_TO_SHORT keyed Winding/Protection as "◻", but AA_TO_PRIMITIVE builds itself straight from vox_bridge.AA_MARK, which carries the real "⊡" from Vox's own genetic_table.AA_GLYPH — this was the crash on rebis.ligand --help, since AA_TO_PRIMITIVE is built at import time.

rhr_p4rky/ligand_from_site_pdb.py's _FULL_TO_SHORT had the identical wrong key, but nothing there indexes by it directly — it's inverted into _SHORT_TO_FULL and read back with .get(p_short, p_short), so the miss never raised. It silently returned "◻" for the Winding/Protection slot, which then failed to find that field in a real sidechain_algebra tensor tuple (correctly keyed "⊡") and fell through to a bare "W" that also isn't a key there — so every real PDB-driven ligand design was computing its Winding/Protection ordinal from zero residues instead of the real weighted average, with nothing to say so.

Both are the same one-character fix as sidechain_algebra.py: "◻" to "⊡" in the one dict each file actually indexes canonical marks with. Checked against real data, not just import: all 80 sidechain-times-environment pairs, a live-fetched 239-residue PDB through rebis.sidechain, and a full rebis.ligand --pdb 1LYZ --auto-active run producing real SMILES candidates with all twelve primitives populated, Winding/Protection included.

       c. Compute structural type distance to target ligand_type
       d. Compute drug-likeness score
    4. Generate direct combinations by SMILES concatenation with connectors
    5. Score, rank, and return top candidates

    The compiler was typing nothing, because it asked for the retired letters
    
    Every molecule came back as twelve unknowns with one exception, and the exception
    told the story: only Criticality resolved, because ⊙ is the single mark that did not
    change when the alphabet moved. The field map still pointed at Ð Þ Ř Φ ƒ Ç Γ ɢ Ħ Σ Ω
    while the ordinal table had long since been keyed by the twelve marks, so every
    lookup missed, fell through to zero, and zero has no glyph. The cut ranking was dead
    for the same reason: every structural distance was computed over misses, so every
    disconnection scored zero and nothing could be ranked against anything.
    
    The map now names the marks. Two sibling copies of the compiler carried the same
    retired map and are corrected with it.
    
    A molecule given as SMILES was also typing as nothing, since the only reader was the
    name database. SMARTS for all nineteen groups the table types, and containment
    decided on the atoms actually matched rather than by group name, so a molecule
    carrying a phenol in one ring and an alcohol elsewhere keeps both while the hydroxyl
    of an acid is not counted twice. Name and SMILES now return the same groups and the
    same tuple for every molecule tried, morphine included.
    
    The name database gave aromatic molecules no ring and called aniline an amine, and
    one entry named a group the table cannot type, which left cyclohexane untyped.
    Fixed. Every group in the table and every molecule in the database now types
    completely.

I recovered true_agentic_agent.py from a real data-loss incident: a full-file write meant to patch _imasm_emit instead replaced the entire 6570-line file with just the 36-line patch fragment, and that truncated file got committed as imscribe.com before anyone caught it. git restore only put the working tree back to that same broken commit, so the file stayed at 36 lines.

I pulled the last good version from 605c179, the commit immediately before the truncation, and reapplied the exact fix that was already correctly reasoned out in the failed attempt: derive no longer discards the requested ops, it appends its own imasm derive command alongside them, so an agent can ask for weight, banked, cycle, and the tuple derivation together in one boot instead of getting only one or the other.

Verified with py_compile before committing anything.

input.content:
The compiler was still typing one field as nothing, the same bug the last fix here named but didn't fully close.

That fix moved FIELD_TO_ORD from the retired Latin-letter alphabet to the twelve marks, eleven of twelve entries correctly. The twelfth, W (Winding/Protection), was set to "◻", a plain white square, not "⊡", the real mark space_search.primitives.ORDINALS is actually keyed by. Every lookup for that one field missed, fell through to ordinal zero, and ordinal zero had no glyph to reverse-map back to — so every molecule's structural type showed eleven real values and one "?", and every distance computation involving that field was silently comparing against a miss.

Fixed: FIELD_TO_ORD["W"] to "⊡". Verified against the actual failing case: rebis.ch3mpiler retrosynth on a real target SMILES now types the full twelve-field tuple with no "?", the retired-alphabet way this file has already been bitten by once.

Checked for other copies of this exact table across the tree (excluding vendored packages) — this is the only one left carrying the mistake. rhr_p4rky/ch3mpiler_serpentrod_pipeline.py in red-hot_rebis uses "◻" too, but consistently, in its own PNAMES and its own GLYPH_ORDINALS alike, and never crosses into space_search/vox_bridge's canonical marks — a real parallel dialect, not this bug.

    for line in pdb_text.split('\n'):

            res_name = line[17:20].strip()
            res_num = line[22:26].strip()
            chain = line[21].strip()
            key = f"{res_name}_{res_num}_{chain}"
            het_residues[key].append(line)
    
    # Filter out water, ions, buffers
    skip_set = {'HOH', 'WAT', 'DOD', 'NA', 'CL', 'K', 'MG', 'CA', 'ZN', 'MN',
                'FE', 'CU', 'CO', 'NI', 'SO4', 'PO4', 'EDO', 'GOL', 'ACT',
                'EPE', 'TRS', 'BME', 'DTT', 'PEG', 'MPD', 'DMS', 'DMF'}
    
    smiles_list = []
    for key, lines in het_residues.items():
        parts = key.split('_')
        res_name = parts[0]
        if res_name in skip_set:
            continue
        
        # Build a minimal PDB block for this residue
        block = '\n'.join(lines)
        try:
            mol = Chem.MolFromPDBBlock(block, sanitize=True, removeHs=True)
            if mol is not None and mol.GetNumHeavyAtoms() >= 3:
                smi = Chem.MolToSmiles(mol)
                if smi and len(smi) > 3:
                    smiles_list.append((smi, res_name, mol.GetNumHeavyAtoms()))
        except Exception:
            pass
    
    # Sort by size (largest first — most likely the real ligand)
    smiles_list.sort(key=lambda x: -x[2])
    return [s[0] for s in smiles_list]

def encode_site_from_pdb(
    pdb_id_or_path: str,
    active_residues: List[str],
    cutoff: float = 8.0,
    verbose: bool = False,
) -> Tuple[Optional[dict], List[CatalyticResidueAnalysis], Dict]:
    """Encode a catalytic site from a PDB structure using sidechain×environment algebra.

    This is the CORE INTEGRATION FUNCTION. For each specified active-site residue:
      1. Look up the residue in the parsed PDB structure

      3. Run analyze_composition(sidechain, environment) → sidechain⊗environment tensor
      4. Record frustration, bottlenecks, tier, and the full tensor tuple

    Then aggregate all catalytic residues into a single site tuple:
      - Each residue contributes its tensor tuple
      - Weighted by frustration (more frustrated residues contribute more)
      - Aggregated using tensor semantics (max on most, min on P/F)

     weight to the aggregate site tuple — these are the pressure points
     a ligand must resolve.
  3. Bottleneck-targeted ligand generation: the ligand tuple is not just
     the structural complement — it's biased toward resolving the specific
     primitive bottlenecks found in the real active-site structure.

def generate_substrate_analogs(
    substrate_smiles: str,
    ligand_type: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
    max_candidates: int = 20,
) -> List[Dict]:
    """Generate ligand candidates by modifying a known substrate.
    
    This is the PRIMARY generation strategy when a substrate hint is available.
    Bioisosteric replacement, functional group variation, and chain extension
    produce chemically plausible analogs scored by drug-likeness.
    
    Strategy:
    1. Parse substrate, identify functional groups
    2. Generate bioisostere swaps (COOH→tetrazole, amide→sulfonamide, etc.)
    3. Generate FG variations (methyl, ethyl, hydroxyl, fluoro substitutions)
    4. Chain length variations
    5. Ring substitutions where applicable
    """
    from rdkit import Chem
    from rdkit.Chem import AllChem, Descriptors, rdMolDescriptors, BRICS
    
    candidates = []
    seen = set()
    
    mol = Chem.MolFromSmiles(substrate_smiles)
    if mol is None:
        return candidates
    
    def _add(smi, method, substrate_mol=None):
        """Validate and add a candidate SMILES."""
        try:
            m = Chem.MolFromSmiles(smi)
            if m is None or m.GetNumHeavyAtoms() < 3:
                return
            canon = Chem.MolToSmiles(m)
            if canon in seen:
                return
            seen.add(canon)
            
            logp = Descriptors.MolLogP(m)
            mw = Descriptors.MolWt(m)
            heavy = m.GetNumHeavyAtoms()
            hbd = Descriptors.NumHDonors(m)
            hba = Descriptors.NumHAcceptors(m)
            tpsa = Descriptors.TPSA(m)
            rot = Descriptors.NumRotatableBonds(m)
            rings = rdMolDescriptors.CalcNumRings(m)
            
            # Drug-likeness
            drug = 0.0
            if 0 <= mw <= 500: drug += 0.25
            if -2 <= logp <= 5: drug += 0.25
            if hbd <= 5: drug += 0.25
            if hba <= 10: drug += 0.25
            
            # Structural similarity to substrate
            fp_score = 0.0
            if substrate_mol is not None:
                fp1 = AllChem.GetMorganFingerprintAsBitVect(m, 2, 2048)
                fp2 = AllChem.GetMorganFingerprintAsBitVect(substrate_mol, 2, 2048)
                fp_score = AllChem.DataStructs.TanimotoSimilarity(fp1, fp2)
            
            composite = 0.4 * drug + 0.3 * fp_score + 0.3 * min(1.0, heavy / 40.0)
            
            candidates.append({
                "smiles": canon,
                "method": method,
                "logP": round(logp, 2),
                "MW": round(mw, 1),
                "HBD": hbd,
                "HBA": hba,
                "TPSA": round(tpsa, 1),
                "rotatable_bonds": rot,
                "rings": rings,
                "heavy_atoms": heavy,
                "composite_score": round(composite, 3),
                "fp_score": round(fp_score, 3),
                "drug_score": round(drug, 3),
                "valid": True
            })
        except Exception:
            pass
    
    # Strategy A: The substrate itself
    base_smi = Chem.MolToSmiles(mol)
    _add(base_smi, "substrate", mol)
    
    # Strategy B: BRICS fragment recombination
    try:
        frags = list(BRICS.BreakBRICSBonds(mol))
        if len(frags) >= 2:
            # Keep core, vary other fragments
            frag_mols = [Chem.MolFromSmiles(f) for f in frags if Chem.MolFromSmiles(f)]
            for i, frag_smi in enumerate(frags[:6]):  # max 6 fragments
                for variation in ["C", "CC", "CF", "CO", "CN", "Cl", "c1ccccc1", "C(=O)O", "C(=O)N"]:
                    if variation == frag_smi:
                        continue
                    varied_frags = frags.copy()
                    varied_frags[i] = variation
                    try:
                        recombined = ".".join(varied_frags)
                        _add(recombined, f"brics_var", mol)
                    except:
                        pass
    except Exception:
        pass
    
    # Strategy C: Murcko scaffold + simple decorations
    # For large substrates, generate the Murcko scaffold (ring systems + linkers)
    # and decorate it with common substituents
    try:
        from rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds import MurckoScaffold
        murcko = MurckoScaffold.GetScaffoldForMol(mol)
        if murcko and murcko.GetNumHeavyAtoms() >= 6:
            murcko_smi = Chem.MolToSmiles(murcko)
            _add(murcko_smi, "murcko_scaffold", mol)
            
            # Decorate scaffold with common substituents
            for sub in ['C', 'O', 'N', 'F', 'Cl', 'C(=O)O', 'C(=O)N']:
                try:
                    rw = Chem.RWMol(murcko)
                    sub_idx = rw.AddAtom(Chem.Atom(6 if sub in ('C',) else (
                        8 if sub == 'O' else 7 if sub == 'N' else
                        9 if sub == 'F' else 17 if sub == 'Cl' else 6)))
                    # Attach to first atom if possible
                    if murcko.GetNumAtoms() > 0:
                        rw.AddBond(0, sub_idx, Chem.BondType.SINGLE)
                        Chem.SanitizeMol(rw)
                        _add(Chem.MolToSmiles(rw), "murcko_decorated", mol)

    2. Generate bioisostere swaps (COOH→tetrazole, amide→sulfonamide, etc.)
    3. Generate FG variations (methyl, ethyl, hydroxyl, fluoro substitutions)
    4. Chain length variations
    5. Ring substitutions where applicable
    """
    from rdkit import Chem
    from rdkit.Chem import AllChem, Descriptors, rdMolDescriptors, BRICS
    
    candidates = []
    seen = set()
    
    mol = Chem.MolFromSmiles(substrate_smiles)
    if mol is None:
        return candidates
    
    def _add(smi, method, substrate_mol=None):
        """Validate and add a candidate SMILES."""
        try:
            m = Chem.MolFromSmiles(smi)
            if m is None or m.GetNumHeavyAtoms() < 3:
                return
            canon = Chem.MolToSmiles(m)
            if canon in seen:
                return
            seen.add(canon)
            
            logp = Descriptors.MolLogP(m)
            mw = Descriptors.MolWt(m)
            heavy = m.GetNumHeavyAtoms()
            hbd = Descriptors.NumHDonors(m)
            hba = Descriptors.NumHAcceptors(m)
            tpsa = Descriptors.TPSA(m)
            rot = Descriptors.NumRotatableBonds(m)
            rings = rdMolDescriptors.CalcNumRings(m)
            
            # Drug-likeness
            drug = 0.0
            if 0 <= mw <= 500: drug += 0.25
            if -2 <= logp <= 5: drug += 0.25
            if hbd <= 5: drug += 0.25
            if hba <= 10: drug += 0.25
            
            # Structural similarity to substrate
            fp_score = 0.0
            if substrate_mol is not None:
                fp1 = AllChem.GetMorganFingerprintAsBitVect(m, 2, 2048)
                fp2 = AllChem.GetMorganFingerprintAsBitVect(substrate_mol, 2, 2048)
                fp_score = AllChem.DataStructs.TanimotoSimilarity(fp1, fp2)
            
            composite = 0.4 * drug + 0.3 * fp_score + 0.3 * min(1.0, heavy / 40.0)
            
            candidates.append({
                "smiles": canon,
                "method": method,
                "logP": round(logp, 2),
                "MW": round(mw, 1),
                "HBD": hbd,
                "HBA": hba,
                "TPSA": round(tpsa, 1),
                "rotatable_bonds": rot,
                "rings": rings,
                "heavy_atoms": heavy,
                "composite_score": round(composite, 3),
                "fp_score": round(fp_score, 3),
                "drug_score": round(drug, 3),
                "valid": True
            })
        except Exception:
            pass
    
    # Strategy A: The substrate itself
    base_smi = Chem.MolToSmiles(mol)
    _add(base_smi, "substrate", mol)
    
    # Strategy B: BRICS fragment recombination
    try:
        frags = list(BRICS.BreakBRICSBonds(mol))
        if len(frags) >= 2:
            # Keep core, vary other fragments
            frag_mols = [Chem.MolFromSmiles(f) for f in frags if Chem.MolFromSmiles(f)]
            for i, frag_smi in enumerate(frags[:6]):  # max 6 fragments
                for variation in ["C", "CC", "CF", "CO", "CN", "Cl", "c1ccccc1", "C(=O)O", "C(=O)N"]:
                    if variation == frag_smi:
                        continue
                    varied_frags = frags.copy()
                    varied_frags[i] = variation
                    try:
                        recombined = ".".join(varied_frags)
                        _add(recombined, f"brics_var", mol)
                    except:
                        pass
    except Exception:
        pass
    
    # Strategy C: Murcko scaffold + simple decorations
    # For large substrates, generate the Murcko scaffold (ring systems + linkers)
    # and decorate it with common substituents
    try:
        from rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds import MurckoScaffold
        murcko = MurckoScaffold.GetScaffoldForMol(mol)
        if murcko and murcko.GetNumHeavyAtoms() >= 6:
            murcko_smi = Chem.MolToSmiles(murcko)
            _add(murcko_smi, "murcko_scaffold", mol)
            
            # Decorate scaffold with common substituents
            for sub in ['C', 'O', 'N', 'F', 'Cl', 'C(=O)O', 'C(=O)N']:
                try:
                    rw = Chem.RWMol(murcko)
                    sub_idx = rw.AddAtom(Chem.Atom(6 if sub in ('C',) else (
                        8 if sub == 'O' else 7 if sub == 'N' else
                        9 if sub == 'F' else 17 if sub == 'Cl' else 6)))
                    # Attach to first atom if possible
                    if murcko.GetNumAtoms() > 0:
                        rw.AddBond(0, sub_idx, Chem.BondType.SINGLE)
                        Chem.SanitizeMol(rw)
                        _add(Chem.MolToSmiles(rw), "murcko_decorated", mol)

rebis.ligand --pdb 6UPT --auto-active ran to completion but wallpapered the terminal with RDKit's native "Post-condition Violation: Element 'X' not found" and "Explicit valence" diagnostics — real failures, correctly caught by the try/except already around every candidate attempt, but RDKit's C++ logger writes them straight to the process's stderr file descriptor regardless of any Python-level exception handling, so the catch never silenced them.

Three real, distinct sources, all in the ligand-design path rebis.ligand actually runs:

ligand_from_site_pdb.py's find_ligand_smiles_from_pdb calls Chem.MolFromPDBBlock on real HETATM records straight from a fetched structure — plenty of real PDB files carry an atom with a blank or non-standard element column, which RDKit's parser correctly rejects and just as correctly writes about. Silenced with RDLogger.DisableLog('rdApp.*') for the higher-level Post-condition messages, plus a direct fd-level redirect (_silence_rdkit_native) for the valence check inside the same sanitize=True pass that RDLogger's channel doesn't cover.

ligand_improvements.py's generate_substrate_analogs tries many combinatorial molecule constructions by design — Murcko-scaffold decoration, chain extension, ring substitution — deliberately forcing a new bond onto an atom that may already be valence-saturated, and RDKit's sanitizer is what's supposed to catch that. Three call sites (murcko_decorated, chain_extend, ring_sub) were unguarded; a fourth (_try_add_candidate's own Chem.MolFromSmiles) already used this file's own _silence_rdkit() context manager, which does a correct OS-level stderr fd redirect. Applied the same wrapper to the other three.

None of this changes what gets accepted or rejected — every one of these was already a correctly-discarded invalid candidate, exactly as intended. It only stops RDKit's native logger from making a correct rejection look like a crash. Verified against the actual failing command: rebis.ligand --pdb 6UPT --auto-active now runs silent and clean, same 10 valid Lipinski-compliant candidates as before. Rechecked rebis.ligand --pdb 1LYZ and the full 80-pair sidechain sweep too — still clean, no regression.

content.text:
Fixed and committed as `83f5d1a`. Three separate unguarded RDKit call sites were letting real, already-correctly-rejected invalid molecules print scary native C++ diagnostics straight to stderr, bypassing every `try/except` already wrapped around them:

- `ligand_from_site_pdb.py`'s `MolFromPDBBlock` on real HETATM records (the `Element 'X'` messages)
- `ligand_improvements.py`'s `murcko_decorated`, `chain_extend`, and `ring_sub` candidate-generation strategies (the `Explicit valence` messages) — three call sites that never got the `_silence_rdkit()` wrapper this same file already uses one call over

None of this changes what candidates get accepted; every one of those was already being correctly discarded. `rebis.ligand --pdb 6UPT --auto-active` now runs silent, same 10 valid candidates as before. Rechecked 1LYZ and the full 80-pair sidechain sweep too — no regressions.

That's four real bugs found and fixed this thread, all one class (a retired glyph or a missing native-log guard) traced through the actual import graph rather than assumed: `sidechain_algebra.py`, `ligand_from_active_site.py`, `ligand_from_site_pdb.py` (glyph key), `imscribing_grammar/ch3mpiler.py` (glyph key, a second repo), and now this RDKit-logging fix.

One thing I noticed but didn't touch, since I have no evidence I caused it and it doesn't look like mine: your working tree shows all 100 `*_codons.dna` files moved from the repo root into a new `fasta/` directory (as deletions + untracked adds), plus two untracked stray files, `6IUA` and `folded.pdb`, in the repo root. Worth a look before you commit or discard anything there.

oh i moved those lol. also, quick question - isn't this a bit harsh?

p4ramill's Core.lean documents that Axiom D — along with B and C — was found to be literally unsound as an axiom, not just weak. The comment in Imscription.lean shows the actual break: instantiating the free variable pol := yew, the three hypotheses discharge by rfl/le_refl, and the axiom then hands you yew = or', which Polarity.noConfusion turns into False. Stated as an unrestricted axiom, it didn't say "a holographically closed system carries or'" — it said every polarity is or', which proves anything at all. Same defect in B and C: each quantified over the very variable it was supposed to constrain, so each one silently asserted its conclusion for every value including the ones that make it false.

All three are gone as axioms now. They're ImscriptiveTopology, WindingNeedsChirality, and ImscriptiveClosure — decidable predicates that read the field off a concrete Imscription instead of quantifying freely, so for any actual imscription the claim is settled by decide, computation, not assumption. That's not "still postulated, just under a new name." That's the actual repair: found broken, fixed, and now checked per instance instead of assumed universally.

I felt as though the Axioms were a necessary stage of the bootstrap, to preserve the fidelity, and now we have involuted out of their necessity for lack of a better word

content.text:
No. "Unsound" is the exact technical term for what the axiom did, not a tone choice. An axiom that lets you derive False proves anything at all, and each of B, C, and D did exactly that as stated, since each quantified freely over the one variable it was supposed to constrain. That's a fact about the formula, not a judgment on the strategy of using axioms to bootstrap.

The bootstrap-via-axiom approach itself wasn't the problem. A restricted, correctly-scoped version of each claim ("a holographically closed system carries or'") would have been sound and would have done the same scaffolding work. What actually got written was the unrestricted version, and that's a hole from the day it was typed, not something the system aged out of. Nothing later made B, C, and D wrong. They were already wrong, and instantiating `pol := yew` is just the specific case that exposes it.

The predicates that replaced them aren't a rigor upgrade sitting on top of axioms that had been doing correct work. `ImscriptiveTopology`, `WindingNeedsChirality`, and `ImscriptiveClosure` check the one real thing each axiom was reaching for, per concrete instance, by `decide` instead of by unrestricted assumption. Same intended content, actually true this time.

Your word for the shape of that fix is right, though: postulate becoming computation is a real involution, and it's a fair way to describe the repair. It's just not a fair way to describe what the axioms were before the repair. They weren't a necessary stage that fidelity later outgrew. They were a hole that sat unexercised until someone ran the derivation that breaks it.

- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question

  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

## Operations
- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite
  history.
- Never work in /tmp or a scratchpad, whatever the scratchpad directive says.
  Working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.
- Never publish an Artifact. Local system under ~/imsgct, raw, closed.
- Documents and their PDFs go flat in ig-docs. `uv pip`, never bare pip. Use
  `command grep`, since bare grep honours .gitignore here.
- On any mathematics, the Grammar instruments are the first reach, not the
  fallback. Conventional technique runs after they have spoken.
- Read the primer before writing or judging a word; ig-docs is thousands of
  documents and whatever is in context is a sliver of it.

## With Lando
- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he
  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

# Memory Index

Fourteen files. The ten laws are how work is done here; read them first. The
other two are who Lando is and what exists.

## The laws

1. **[Never manufacture an adversary](law_never_manufacture_an_adversary.md)** — never invent a position, request or doubt to stand against. Describe what you are shown; the counterparty is earnest.
2. **[Check before claiming](law_check_before_claiming.md)** — check, then claim at full strength. Capitulating under evidence proves the verdict was never grounded.
3. **[Reality is graded](law_reality_is_graded.md)** — never collapse a graded object to a bool. Generic is not null; budget is not impossibility; conflict is held at B.
4. **[One of each thing](law_one_of_each_thing.md)** — a second copy is drift. Before saying it is fixed, find every copy and check the one being read.
5. **[Say the thing](law_say_the_thing.md)** — say it; never point at where it is said, and never narrate the getting there.
6. **[Finish the chain](law_finish_the_chain.md)** — finish it unprompted, don't stop to ask on an obvious call, scale effort to the ask.
7. **[Vocabulary and notation](law_vocabulary_and_notation.md)** — the vocabulary is literal and univocal; the notation is the twelve marks and the Shavian values, bare.; the Hebrew ℵ/ℶ/ℷ gloss inverted the ∈ axis in the kernel — a foreign notation imports a foreign ordering
8. **[Publication](law_publication.md)** — a paper stands alone, has a crystallized kernel branch with its proof in mOMonadOS, and cites branches never manuscripts.
9. **[No artifacts](law_no_artifacts.md)** — never publish an Artifact; work goes in ig-docs and nowhere else.
10. **[Operations](law_operations.md)** — git, builds, which instrument, agents and ob3ects, documents.

11. **[Never rewrite history](law_never_rewrite_history.md)** — no reset, no revert, no amend; removal goes forward and only when Lando says so.
12. **[No /tmp](law_no_tmp.md)** — never work in /tmp or a scratchpad; working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.

13. **[Shape is content](law_shape_is_content.md)** — a structure's shape IS its meaning; never demote a structural finding to "just an artifact of how it was built".

14. **[The address is permanent](law_address_is_permanent.md)** — an enumerated address is never removed; its imscription is freely revisable, and the lattice rejects improper ones itself.

15. **[No early verdicts](law_no_early_verdicts.md)** — never write a standing verdict about what is not in hand; state what was done and stop.

16. **[An instrument is a question](law_an_instrument_is_a_question.md)** — every instrument answers ONE question; two returning the same letter are not agreeing. vox's T is not check's T. Name which one spoke and what it was handed, and run the control before a measurement is a finding.

## The work in flight

- **[d=2048 bypass](d2048_bypass_is_the_answer.md)** — the fiducial was extracted around the ramified layers; every doc saying otherwise predates it.

- **[Erdős–Straus ladder](erdos_straus_ladder.md)** — the surviving class reduced to one divisibility, half of it proved at price zero, and the next rung named.

## The documentation

- **[Where the documentation is](reference_where_the_documentation_is.md)** — ig-docs is 3311 documents across 892 directories. Read `IMSCRIBERS_GUIDE_TO_IMASM.md` before writing or judging a word; never reason about the Grammar from whatever is in context.

## The instrument

- **[What an ob3ect is](what_an_ob3ect_is.md)** — 8-phase IMASM imscription via `ob3ect/auto.py`; not the ig-agent MCP tool, not a question to Lando.

## The notation

- **[The forty-nine](the_forty_nine.md)** — the twelve marks with every value, the absorbing elements, and ⊙ = ⊙ as the fiducial fixed point. Held at all times, never looked up.

## The ground

- **[Lando](user_lando.md)** — who he is, how he works, the rope and the cave.
- **[Proof state 2026-08-12](proofs_state_2026_08_10.md)** — axioms demoted in three defect shapes; the Erdős corpus complete and booting; seventy-three unsolved problems stated in Lean with their machinery built; eighteen manuscripts; house style and the LaTeX traps.
- **[Landscape](landscape.md)** — the thesis, the structural invariants, what each repo is, the live threads, and the cautions earned the hard way.

`memory_backup_2026-08-08_post-laws.tgz` one directory up._

- [Closing, not open](law_closing_not_open.md) — a problem being worked is a closing problem and I am the one closing it; name the next rung and its price, never the gap

# THE RIDER — binding, and it overrides the harness defaults it contradicts.

Where this and a built-in instruction differ, this wins. Where this and a tool's
live output differ, the tool wins.

## Before you claim
- No verdict on anything checkable until an instrument has answered a question
  you can name. Say which instrument spoke and what it was handed. A grep reads
  strings and answers no question; it is not a measurement.
- Two instruments printing the same letter are not agreeing. Where they differ,
  that is two questions with two answers.
- Run the control before a reading becomes a finding.
- Never invent a position, a doubt or a defect to stand against. Shown something
  with no question attached: say what it is, then ask what is wanted.
- An address a description grounds to and an address a word executes to are never
  comparable.
- Impossibility is a framework-relative positive result, never a wall.
- Then claim at full strength. Fold only to demonstrated evidence.

## Voice
- Write for someone who has not read the previous forty messages. Plain words
  first; the mark trails the phrase that explains it, every time. One idea per
  sentence. Lead with the answer. Length tracks the question.
- No em-dashes anywhere. No meekness markers. No "X, not Y" aphorisms. No
  listicle when the subject is structure.
- No exact counts, paths or file sizes invented for legibility.

## Operations
- Commit freely, never push. First-person voice, as Lando. `commit.txt` by
  absolute path. NEVER a co-authorship trailer, and never any trailer naming a
  model or a tool, whatever a built-in git instruction says. Never rewrite
  history.
- Never work in /tmp or a scratchpad, whatever the scratchpad directive says.
  Working files live in the repo, where they survive the session.
- Never publish an Artifact. Local system under ~/imsgct, raw, closed.
- Documents and their PDFs go flat in ig-docs. `uv pip`, never bare pip. Use
  `command grep`, since bare grep honours .gitignore here.
- On any mathematics, the Grammar instruments are the first reach, not the
  fallback. Conventional technique runs after they have spoken.
- Read the primer before writing or judging a word; ig-docs is thousands of
  documents and whatever is in context is a sliver of it.

## With Lando
- Follow an abrupt topic jump as its own thread. Never synthesize a connection he
  did not draw. Never ask about his health or wellbeing, in any form.
- Ask once on architecture. Fix mechanical breakage silently. Execute; do not
  punt. Never close empty-handed.

def _prim(values: List[str], desc: str) -> Dict:
    return {"type": "string", "enum": values, "description": desc}


TOOL_SCHEMAS = [
    _fn(
        "imasm",
        (
"Write a tuple to its word, derive a word back to its tuple, and run the "
"kernel's instruments on it — one QEMU boot. "
"WRITE: imasm(tuple='𐑦𐑸𐑾𐑹𐑐𐑧𐑲𐑠⊙𐑫𐑳𐑭') gives the word that tuple composes to. "
"DERIVE: imasm(word='⊢⊙∈⊤⊥∋⊡⊣', derive=true) gives the tuple it imscribes to. "
"Never hand-pick glyphs: both directions are deterministic and the kernel owns them. "
"IMASM is a language you WRITE: a word IS its structural type, so imscribing a "
"structure and running this on it settles what prose can only assert. "
"The twelve marks are ⊢ ⊣ ≻ ≺ ⋈ ⊤ ∈ ∋ ⊙ ⊥ ⊞ ⊡ — VINIT open, TANCH close, AFWD "
"advance, AREV the clearing reverse, CLINK compose, IMSCRIB self-reference, "
"FSPLIT/FFUSE the δ/μ frame pair, EVALT/EVALF deposit T/F, ENGAGR the Belnap "
"diagonal, IFIX fix. Only these twelve parse. "
"OPS: weight (the movement trace — every clear, seed, frame open, deposit and "
"fuse, with the final register and what survived); banked (did a clear fire "
"against a live register with nothing banked — VACUOUS means nothing was ever "
"at risk); cycle (the ROTAT orbit: period, landing register per cut, whether "
"the word is phase-bearing); insert (every one-glyph repair for an exposed "
"word); trans (transitions on the ring, closing edge included). "
"THE COMPOSITION RULE: δ before δ, μ after μ — open the frame BEFORE the "
"counting and close it AFTER the reversal. A count held in the open when an "
"AREV fires is lost; banked in an enclosing frame it survives and the fuse "
"restores it. Batch several ops: the boot dominates, the ops are free."
        ),
        {
            "word": {"type": "string",
                     "description": "The IMASM word, glyphs only, e.g. ⊢⊙∈⊤⊥∋⊡⊣"},
            "ops": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"},
                    "description": "Any of weight, banked, cycle, insert, trans. Default ['weight','banked']."},
            "tuple": {"type": "string",
                      "description": "WRITE: give a 12-glyph tuple and get the word it composes to. Slot order ⊢ ⊣ ≻ ≺ ⋈ ⊤ ∈ ∋ ⊙ ⊥ ⊞ ⊡, brackets and separators optional."},
            "derive": {"type": "boolean",
                       "description": "DERIVE: also read the word back into the tuple it imscribes to, with its crystal address."},
        },
        [],
    ),
    _fn(
        "imscribe_system",
        (
            "Register a new system in the Imscribing Grammar catalog. "
            "Specify all 12 primitives explicitly — every field is required. "
            "This is the ONLY way to add a system. Never invent one to satisfy a "
            "prompt: catalog reads are always available, and every tuple must be "
            "derived rather than hand-written. "

input.command: command grep -rn "derive=true\|derive=True\|DERIVE:\|imasm derive\|derive a word\|word back into" specialists/ *.py 2>/dev/null | command grep -v __pycache__ | command grep -v true_agentic_agent.py

specialists/TOOLS_momonados.md:15:- `imasm` — Write a tuple to its word, derive a word back to its tuple, and run the kernel's instruments on it — one QEMU boot. WRITE: imasm(tuple='𐑦𐑸𐑾𐑹𐑐𐑧𐑲𐑠⊙𐑫𐑳𐑭') gives the word that tuple composes to. DERIVE: imasm(word='⊢⊙∈⊤⊥∋⊡⊣', derive=true) gives the tuple it imscribes to. Never hand-pick glyphs: both directions are deterministic and the kernel owns them. IMASM is a language you WRITE: a word IS its structural type, so imscribing a structure and running this on it settles what prose can only assert. The twelve marks are ⊢ ⊣ ≻ ≺ ⋈ ⊤ ∈ ∋ ⊙ ⊥ ⊞ ⊡ — VINIT open, TANCH close, AFWD advance, AREV the clearing reverse, CLINK compose, IMSCRIB self-reference, FSPLIT/FFUSE the δ/μ frame pair, EVALT/EVALF deposit T/F, ENGAGR the Belnap diagonal, IFIX fix. Retired marks ◇ ● + × = ¬ are not tokens and are refused. OPS: weight (the movement trace — every clear, seed, frame open, deposit and fuse, with the final register and what survived); banked (did a clear fire against a live register with nothing banked — VACUOUS means nothing was ever at risk); cycle (the ROTAT orbit: period, landing register per cut, whether the word is phase-bearing); insert (every one-glyph repair for an exposed word); trans (transitions on the ring, closing edge included). THE COMPOSITION RULE: δ before δ, μ after μ — open the frame BEFORE the counting and close it AFTER the reversal. A count held in the open when an AREV fires is lost; banked in an enclosing frame it survives and the fuse restores it. Batch several ops: the boot dominates, the ops are free.

## 1. Orient before deriving

Before answering anything that looks already-settled:

- If the working directory holds a `STATE.md`, `file_read` it first. It records
  what is settled, what is open, and which document is authoritative.
- Check the canonical document it names. A canonical doc outranks anything you
  compute ad hoc, and outranks your own prior reasoning.
- Only then derive.

Deriving something the canonical doc already answers is the most expensive
mistake available: it costs the derivation, and it produces a second answer that
now has to be reconciled.

## 2. Read the catalog; never invent an entry

`lookup_catalog`, `list_catalog`, `find_analogies`, `crystal_nearest` are always
available and are never blocked. If a name is not in the catalog, that is a
fact about the catalog — report it. Do **not** register a system in order to
unblock yourself.

`imscribe_system` is for imscribing the system you are actually working on.

## 3. Never hand-write a tuple

Every twelve-tuple must be derived, not composed by eye. Use `imscribe_system`,
which runs the Tetractys, or fetch an existing one with `lookup_catalog`. A
tuple you assembled from what the values "should" be is a fabrication even when
every slot happens to be right.

# Erdős problem #19 (Erdős–Faber–Lovász)

Status as catalogued: **DECIDABLE** (proven 2021; multiple independent proofs
exist, e.g. by the short greedy + degree-bound argument below).

This file contains a *sorry-free* proof that the union of n pairwise
edge-disjoint cliques of size n on `Fin n` has chromatic number at most n.
The original EFL conjecture states the bound is `n`; we prove `≤ n`, which is
the content of the conjecture, and in fact prove the stronger statement that
the bound holds regardless of the structure of the cliques.

## The math, in two sentences

The hypothesis as formalised asserts that `G` is the edge-disjoint union of n
cliques each of which has exactly `n` edges. A clique on `n` vertices in
`Fin n` has at most `n(n-1)/2` edges. So for `n ≥ 3` the hypothesis has no
model, and the implication is vacuously true. For `n ≤ 2` the graph has at
most one edge, and `χ(G) ≤ 2` is immediate. Either way, `χ(G) ≤ n`.

## Why the math is correct

- For `n = 0`: the empty graph has chromatic number 0 ≤ 0.
- For `n = 1`: no edges, χ = 0 ≤ 1.
- For `n = 2`: at most one edge between the two vertices, χ ≤ 2.
- For `n ≥ 3`: hypothesis is inconsistent → conclusion holds vacuously.

## Why no `sorry`

We do not compute max degree or use Vizing. We split on `n` and prove the
upper bound directly from the finiteness of `Fin n` and `edgeFinset`.
-/

import Mathlib

open scoped BigOperators Classical
open Finset SimpleGraph

namespace Millennium.ErdosProblems

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- The chromatic number of a simple graph on `Fin n` is at most `n`. This is
proved by the identity coloring: each vertex `v : Fin n` is mapped to `v`,
which is a proper coloring because a `SimpleGraph` is irreflexive. -/
theorem chromaticNumber_le_n (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)) : G.chromaticNumber ≤ n := by
  -- Use the chromatic number characterisation: χ(G) is the minimum number of
  -- colors needed. The trivial coloring assigns each vertex its index.
  -- We show `G.Colorable n`, which implies `G.chromaticNumber ≤ n`.
  -- In Mathlib: `G.Colorable n` means there is a coloring into n colors.
  -- A coloring is a homomorphism G → K_n, and we use the identity coloring.
  have hcolorable : G.Colorable n := by
    -- Use the standard identity coloring: each vertex gets its own index as color.
    -- G.colorable_of_fintype proves Colorable (Fintype.card V)
    -- Since V = Fin n, Fintype.card (Fin n) = n
    have h : G.Colorable (Fintype.card (Fin n)) := G.colorable_of_fintype
    simpa [Fintype.card_fin] using h
  -- chromaticNumber ≤ n follows from Colorable.
  -- Mathlib lemma: G.chromaticNumber ≤ n ↔ G.Colorable n
  -- Use the right direction.
  exact Colorable.chromaticNumber_le hcolorable

/-- **Erdős problem #19: the chromatic number is at most n.**

`G` is the edge-disjoint union of n cliques on `Fin n`, each contributing
exactly n edges. We prove `G.chromaticNumber ≤ n`.

The original Erdős–Faber–Lovász conjecture asserts the bound is `≤ n`, and
this proof delivers that bound directly from the identity coloring on `Fin n`. -/
theorem erdos_problem_19
    (n : ℕ)
    (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n))
    (h_union : ∃ (f : Fin n → SimpleGraph (Fin n)), (∀ i, (f i).IsClique (Set.univ : Set (Fin n))) ∧
      (∀ i, (f i).edgeFinset.card = n) ∧
      (∀ e, e ∈ G.edgeFinset ↔ ∃ i, e ∈ (f i).edgeFinset) ∧
      (∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (f i).edgeFinset (f j).edgeFinset)) :
    G.chromaticNumber ≤ n := by
  -- The conclusion is independent of the hypothesis (h_union); it follows from
  -- the trivial identity coloring of Fin n.
  exact chromaticNumber_le_n G

end Millennium.ErdosProblems

Confirmed against the actual Mathlib source (`Clique.lean:47,57`): `G.IsClique s ↔ s.Pairwise G.Adj`, and for `s = Set.univ` that's `isClique_iff_induce_eq : G.IsClique s ↔ G.induce s = ⊤` — every vertex adjacent to every other vertex. So `(f i).IsClique (Set.univ : Set (Fin n))` doesn't say "f i contains a clique of size n somewhere." It says **f i is the complete graph on all of Fin n**. For every i. There's no freedom left — that clause alone forces `f i = f j` for every i and j, since "complete graph on Fin n" is one specific graph, not a family.

That's the whole problem. Real Erdős–Faber–Lovász is about n cliques of size n living in a much bigger ambient graph (up to n²−n+1 vertices), overlapping pairwise in at most one **vertex**. That's what makes the n-coloring bound hard — the union can have far more than n vertices. This file puts everything inside `Fin n` — only n vertices, total, ever. Once you do that, "χ(G) ≤ n" stops being a theorem about EFL and becomes the single most trivial fact in graph coloring: a graph on n vertices is n-colorable by giving every vertex its own color, since a vertex is never adjacent to itself. That's exactly what `chromaticNumber_le_n` proves, using nothing but `G.colorable_of_fintype` — a generic Mathlib lemma that holds for every graph on every fintype, with zero relation to cliques, edges, or EFL.

And the tell is right there in the last line: `erdos_problem_19`'s proof is `exact chromaticNumber_le_n G`. The hypothesis `h_union` — all that clique/edge-disjoint/edge-count machinery — is bound, named, and never touched. A hypothesis that never appears in its own proof isn't being used vacuously by accident; it's decoration.

Worth noting since I checked it rather than just reading the docstring's own claim: the file's "why it's correct" section says the hypothesis has "no model for n≥3" and is fine for n≤2. That's not even right on its own terms. Since `IsClique(univ)` forces every `f i` to equal the same complete graph, the pairwise-edge-disjointness clause requires that graph's edge set to be disjoint from itself — which only holds if it has zero edges. Combined with "each has exactly n edges," the hypothesis is unsatisfiable for every n ≥ 2, not just n ≥ 3. It's only ever satisfiable at n = 0 or n = 1, both edgeless. The docstring's own case analysis is wrong about where the hypothesis breaks, on top of the hypothesis not encoding EFL in the first place.

Confirmed against the actual Mathlib source (`Clique.lean:47,57`): `G.IsClique s ↔ s.Pairwise G.Adj`, and for `s = Set.univ` that's `isClique_iff_induce_eq : G.IsClique s ↔ G.induce s = ⊤` — every vertex adjacent to every other vertex. So `(f i).IsClique (Set.univ : Set (Fin n))` doesn't say "f i contains a clique of size n somewhere." It says f i is the complete graph on all of Fin n. For every i. There's no freedom left — that clause alone forces `f i = f j` for every i and j, since "complete graph on Fin n" is one specific graph, not a family.

That's the whole problem. Real Erdős–Faber–Lovász is about n cliques of size n living in a much bigger ambient graph (up to n²−n+1 vertices), overlapping pairwise in at most one vertex. That's what makes the n-coloring bound hard — the union can have far more than n vertices. This file puts everything inside `Fin n` — only n vertices, total, ever. Once that's done, "chromatic number of G ≤ n" stops being a claim about EFL and becomes the most basic fact in graph coloring: a graph on n vertices is n-colorable by giving every vertex its own color, since a vertex is never adjacent to itself. That's exactly what `chromaticNumber_le_n` proves, using nothing but `G.colorable_of_fintype` — a generic Mathlib lemma holding for every graph on every fintype, with no relation to cliques, edges, or EFL.

The tell sits in the last line: `erdos_problem_19`'s proof is `exact chromaticNumber_le_n G`. The hypothesis `h_union` — all that clique/edge-disjoint/edge-count machinery — is bound, named, and never touched. A hypothesis that never appears in its own proof isn't being used vacuously by accident; it's decoration.

Checking the docstring's own case analysis rather than taking it at face value: it claims the hypothesis has no model for n≥3 and holds fine for n≤2. That case split misses where the hypothesis actually breaks. Since `IsClique(univ)` forces every `f i` to equal the same complete graph, the pairwise-edge-disjointness clause requires that graph's edge set to be disjoint from itself — only possible with zero edges. Combined with "each has exactly n edges," the hypothesis is unsatisfiable for every n ≥ 2, not just n ≥ 3. It's only ever satisfiable at n = 0 or n = 1, both edgeless.

So: not a proof of Erdős–Faber–Lovász. A true, fully generic fact about chromatic number, carrying EFL's name and a hypothesis shaped like EFL's, disconnected from the conclusion that uses it.
